entries.title: Hub — Sci-fi Pura Vida feel
entries.note: Style translation of a warm reggae pocket into a sci-fi hub dock bed: keep the laid-back groove, replace band instruments with synth/MIDI.
entries.referenceIntent: Stylie — Pura Vida (feel only; not a cover)
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. Warm sci-fi chillwave / downtempo electronic for docking at a hub station, 82 BPM, F sharp minor. Instruments: soft analog polysynth pads, sequenced offbeat synth plucks replacing guitar skank, deep sine sub bass, sparse electronic kit with soft kick and brushed noise hats, distant FM bell motifs. Structure: open on pads and sub only for the first few seconds; pluck arp enters on offbeats; kit settles into a quiet pocket and stays; no drop, no hook, texture mutates slowly. Production: wide stereo, mild sidechain, plate reverb, tape delay on plucks, warm analog glue. Banned: reggae guitar skank, organ church tones, vocals, choir, trailer braams, big EDM drops, catchy lead melody.

entries.title: Battle — Guitar + MIDI guitar
entries.note: Combat elevation of the hub sci-fi / Pura Vida-feel pocket. Lead voice is overdriven electric rhythm guitar plus MIDI/synth-guitar motifs; warm analog family, continuous drive, no drop.
entries.referenceIntent: Same warm pocket as hub_sci_fi_pura_vida_feel_20s, battle intensity
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Driving sci-fi combat bed for a roguelite space shooter battle, same warm analog family as a chillwave hub dock track but elevated into combat, 126 BPM, F sharp minor. Main instruments: overdriven electric guitar with palm-muted rhythm chugs low in the mix, and a MIDI guitar / synth-guitar lead that plays sequenced melodic phrases with mild portamento and tape delay — futuristic, not bluesy, not metal solo wank. Support: deep sine and analog sub bass, sidechained polysynth pads, motorik electronic kit with punchy kick and crisp hats, sparse FM sparkle accents. Structure: open with muted guitar pulse and sub for four seconds; kit and bass lock the pocket; MIDI guitar motif enters and mutates rather than looping a catchy hook; mid-clip add a second guitar layer then strip slightly before the end; continuous drive, no EDM drop, no big chorus payoff. Production: wide stereo, mild sidechain pump, plate reverb, tape saturation, warm analog glue, slightly dusty. Banned: reggae skank, organ church tones, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, vocal chops, shred guitar solos, djent chugs, catchy pop hooks.

entries.title: Battle — Mid-song + space FX
entries.note: Same guitar + MIDI-guitar battle pocket, but starts already mid-arrangement (loopable body, no intro). Background space color: LFO wobble, filter sweeps, Shepard sheens, ring-mod ticks, granular dust, Doppler/telemetry accents.
entries.referenceIntent: Mid-section / loop body of battle_sci_fi_guitar_midi_30s with sci-fi FX bed
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Mid-song excerpt of a driving sci-fi combat bed for a roguelite space shooter — already fully underway, as if you dropped into the middle of the track, not an intro. 126 BPM, F sharp minor. Continuous loopable groove section; no opening build, no ending fade, no drop, no chorus payoff. From the first beat the full arrangement is present: overdriven electric guitar palm-muted rhythm chugs, MIDI guitar / synth-guitar lead motifs with mild portamento and tape delay, deep analog sub bass, sidechained polysynth pads, motorik electronic kit locked in. Signature space sci-fi color in the background throughout: slow LFO wobble bass undertone, resonant filter sweeps, distant Shepard-tone-like rising sheens, soft ring-modulated metallic ticks, granular starfield dust, occasional Doppler whoosh and telemetry blip accents, subtle bitcrush sparkle far back in the mix. These FX sit behind the guitars as atmosphere — never stealing the pocket, never becoming a trailer braam or alarm siren. Texture mutates slowly across the thirty seconds so a loop will not announce a hook; guitars stay the main voice. Production: wide stereo, mild sidechain pump, plate reverb, tape saturation, warm analog glue, slightly dusty. Banned: quiet sparse intro, fade-in, fade-out, reggae skank, organ church tones, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, vocal chops, shred solos, djent, catchy pop hooks, big EDM drop.

entries.title: Battle — Prog dual timescale
entries.note: RoR2-informed translation (no artist names in prompt): slow patient electric guitar lead over fast analog arps/ticks; dirty live-feel drums; open warm mix; mid-song body only.
entries.referenceIntent: Style translation of progressive electronic sci-fi combat beds (dual timescale: slow guitar / fast synth bed)
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Mid-song loopable body of a progressive electronic sci-fi combat bed for a roguelite space shooter, already fully dense from the first beat, as if dropped into the middle of a long prog track — no intro, no ending fade, no EDM drop, no chorus payoff. 128 BPM, F sharp minor. SLOW main voice: electric guitar playing long ascending and sustained motifs with tape delay and plate reverb — patient human phrasing that spans multiple bars, not shredding, not bluesy bends, not palm-mute chug as the lead. Optional light overdriven rhythm guitar sits low under the lead, sparse and supportive. FAST underlayer: analog synth arpeggios in sixteenth-note motion that slowly mutate, plus short metallic synth ticks and filtered noise accents far back. Support: wide analog pads, dirty live-feel acoustic drum kit (sampled but human, not quantised EDM), deep analog bass, sparse electric piano sparkle, one simple distorted synth lead with long reverb that could almost be mistaken for a second guitar. Dual timescale is essential: slow patient guitar over a restless quick electronic bed. Open warm mix, minimal compression, many layers audible at once, 1970s progressive electronic sci-fi warmth, slightly dusty tape saturation. Banned: quiet sparse intro, fade-in, fade-out, reggae skank, organ church tones, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, vocal chops, catchy pop hooks, metal solos, djent chugs, big sidechain EDM drops, naming any commercial artist or game soundtrack.

entries.title: Battle — Sparse to grand solo
entries.note: Three-phase arc: sparse MIDI/synth + random FX → build with keys/perc → grand electric synth-guitar solo with keyboard lines behind and drums coming through.
entries.referenceIntent: Soft sparse atmosphere into grand guitar/keys chorus; more random sci-fi accents
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Progressive electronic sci-fi combat cue for a roguelite space shooter, 128 BPM, F sharp minor, with a clear three-phase arrangement over sixty seconds — sparse, then build, then grand. PHASE 1 (first ~20 seconds): almost empty. Only a few things playing: soft MIDI synth melody far back, gentle analog pad, occasional random sci-fi accents (short metallic ticks, filtered noise blips, tiny telemetry chirps, granular dust). No drums yet, no guitar yet, quiet and patient. PHASE 2 (middle ~15–20 seconds): slowly add layers — soft keyboard / electric piano melody, mutating analog arp, light percussion entering, tension rising, still not full. PHASE 3 (final ~20–25 seconds): GRAND main section / chorus payoff. Hero electric synth-guitar solo — expressive, sustained, ascending, tape delay and plate reverb, not shred-metal, not blues rock. Keyboard / synth solo lines weaving behind and under the guitar. Drums come through clearly now: punchy live-feel kit driving the grand section. Bass and pads swell wide. Keep scattered random FX in the background throughout all phases, but never louder than the melodies. Contrast is the point: soft sparse MIDI atmosphere into a grand guitar-and-keys climax. Production: open warm mix, mild tape saturation, wide stereo, progressive electronic sci-fi. Banned: starting already full, flat energy the whole time, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, djent, pop vocal chops, naming any commercial artist or game soundtrack.

entries.title: Battle — Clean bass drop + held solo
entries.note: 2m clean/crisp take of sparse→build→grand. Explicitly bans static/hiss/noise. Heavy bass drop into grand section; electric synth-guitar solo with long held notes; keys behind; drums in the climax.
entries.referenceIntent: Cleanup of battle_sparse_to_grand_solo_60s + stronger bass drop + longer sustained guitar solo
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Clean, crisp progressive electronic sci-fi combat track for a roguelite space shooter, 128 BPM, F sharp minor, two minutes, polished studio mix. CRITICAL CLEANLINESS: pristine and clear — no static, no hiss, no white noise, no vinyl crackle, no tape hiss, no bitcrush grit, no granular dust wash, no noisy ambience beds. Tight transient drums, clear separation between instruments, modern mastering clarity with warm analog tone but zero noise floor. STRUCTURE over two minutes: 0:00–0:35 SPARSE: only a few clean layers — soft MIDI synth melody, gentle clean analog pad, occasional short clean metallic blips (dry, no noise). No drums, no guitar. Quiet and patient. 0:35–1:05 BUILD: soft keyboard / electric piano melody enters, clean mutating analog arp, light percussion fades in, deep sub bass begins to swell toward a bass drop. 1:05–2:00 GRAND CHORUS / SOLO SECTION: a heavy bass drop lands — deep sub boom into full pocket. Hero electric synth-guitar solo with LONG HELD NOTES — sustained whole-note and half-note phrases, slow expressive bends, long sustain with tape delay and plate reverb tails, patient legato soloing, not fast shredding, not busy runs. Hold notes for bars at a time. Clean keyboard / synth solo lines weave behind the guitar. Punchy live-feel drums come through clearly. Wide pads and powerful bass. Keep sparse clean FX accents only — never noisy. Contrast: soft sparse clean MIDI atmosphere into a grand bass-drop guitar-and-keys climax. Production: open wide stereo, clean high end, solid sub bass, minimal compression artifacts, crisp and polished. Banned: static, hiss, noise washes, bitcrush, vinyl crackle, dusty lo-fi grit, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, djent, naming any commercial artist or game soundtrack.

entries.title: Battle — Clean soft beat + held solo
entries.note: Same clean sparse→bass-drop→held-solo arc as battle_clean_bassdrop_heldsolo_2m, but drums restrained: soft, sparse, evolving, never a loud repetitive beat through the whole track. Bass and melodies carry rhythm.
entries.referenceIntent: Retry of clean 2m with softer less-repetitive percussion
entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Clean, crisp progressive electronic sci-fi combat track for a roguelite space shooter, 128 BPM, F sharp minor, two minutes, polished studio mix. CRITICAL CLEANLINESS: pristine and clear — no static, no hiss, no white noise, no vinyl crackle, no tape hiss, no bitcrush grit, no granular dust wash, no noisy ambience beds. DRUMS / BEAT — IMPORTANT: keep percussion soft, restrained, and non-dominant. Do NOT loop a loud repetitive four-on-the-floor or motorik beat through the whole song. Avoid a strong pounding kick that stays the same for two minutes. Prefer sparse, evolving, lightly mixed drums: soft ghost notes, occasional tom or rim, brushed or distant hats, irregular entries, drums sit behind the melodies. In the sparse section: no drums. In the build: only faint light percussion. In the grand section: drums may support but stay secondary to guitar and bass — never a loud repetitive beat driving the mix. STRUCTURE over two minutes: 0:00–0:35 SPARSE: only a few clean layers — soft MIDI synth melody, gentle clean analog pad, occasional short clean metallic blips (dry, no noise). No drums, no guitar. Quiet and patient. 0:35–1:05 BUILD: soft keyboard / electric piano melody enters, clean mutating analog arp, very light sparse percussion fades in quietly, deep sub bass swells toward a bass drop. 1:05–2:00 GRAND CHORUS / SOLO SECTION: a heavy bass drop lands — deep sub boom into full pocket. Hero electric synth-guitar solo with LONG HELD NOTES — sustained whole-note and half-note phrases, slow expressive bends, long sustain with tape delay and plate reverb tails, patient legato soloing, not fast shredding. Hold notes for bars at a time. Clean keyboard / synth solo lines weave behind the guitar. Soft supportive drums only — low in the mix, varied, not loop-locked. Wide pads and powerful bass carry the rhythm more than the kit. Contrast: soft sparse clean MIDI atmosphere into a grand bass-drop guitar-and-keys climax. Production: open wide stereo, clean high end, solid sub bass, crisp and polished, melodies first. Banned: loud repetitive beat throughout, pounding kick loops, static, hiss, noise washes, bitcrush, vinyl crackle, vocals, choir, trailer braams, orchestral stabs, djent, naming any commercial artist or game soundtrack.

entries.prompt: Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir, no spoken word. Progressive electronic post-rock for a roguelite space shooter, 100 BPM, D minor. Start sparse: one warm analog pad and a distant arpeggiated synth, no drums for the first twenty seconds. Then bring in a live-feel drum kit, soft kick and brushed ride, played by a human rather than quantised. Add fretless bass guitar, clean electric guitar arpeggios through tape delay, and layered polysynth. One long crescendo across the whole track, jazz-tinged extended chords, never resolving into a pop hook. Tape saturation, plate reverb, wide stereo, warm analog glue. No orchestral stabs, no trailer braams, no vocal chops.
